## Verdict: PASS. Q124 is closed with its pin, the refusal count did not rise, and there is no new blocker

## (1) The failing line (Q124), re-run

**The reproduction.** The mirror held the before-image of `rederive.ts` and `pair.test.ts` over the tree's derivation
sources. `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=1 bench/test/determinism/pair.test.ts` gave:

```
AssertionError: junction:6nymg6w713p26: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 ❯ test/determinism/pair.test.ts:86:40
      Tests  1 failed | 8 passed (9)
exit 1
```

So the declared red reproduces exactly as Q124 states: 8 of 9 green, red at `:86`. The same run shows `:77`
(`duplicateIds` 0) and `:78` (`silentRebinds` 0) green **before** the round, because they read the minted addresses.
CONFIRMED.

**The cause, from this checker's own probe** (`zz-closeprobe.test.ts`, mirror only; output
`/home/user/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-d-09/probe-out.txt`). The probe derived the site and fusion pairs at seeds 1 – 4
at the test frame. At site seed 1 it lists the two raw collisions Q124 names:

| old address | successor (distance) | the fresh entity whose own id is that address | its minted address |
|---|---|---|---|
| `junction:6nymg6w713p26` | `junction:3ab8743sbjpay` (74.7 cm) | same lineage `[236050502,1794805815]`, 4 975.5 cm away | `junction:6nymg6w713p26~1` |
| `block:2skgtzs7hxr50` | `block:cmps09px73p0z` (70.2 cm) | same lineage `[1327423648,751704830]`, 4 385.4 cm away | `block:2skgtzs7hxr50~1` |

* **The matcher.** `match` gave each address to the nearest anchor within the hysteresis radius. That is §6.3's
  carry-over as written: "the fresh entity with the same kind and class family whose anchor lies nearest within the
  kind's hysteresis radius succeeds it". `MatchResult.addressOf` is documented in `packages/model/src/match/types.ts`
  as the provisional map: "the handed-on one for a successor, its own for a fresh entity". So the raw map holding the
  natural holder at its own id is the matcher's contract, before the mint. **There is no defect in `match`**, and
  nothing goes to M0-d-05b. CONFIRMED (probe) and PLAUSIBLE (the reading of §6.3).
* **The mint, before the round.** The old `mintAddresses` already started `taken` with every old id. So each natural
  holder of a handed-on address took `~1`: §6.3's "an address its own batch retires takes the suffix `~k`". The
  probe's inline copy of the old mint gives the same final map as the new mint at all eight pairs (`oldMintSame=true`).
  So `duplicateIds` 0 was the true count of the final addresses, not a blind spot. CONFIRMED.
* **So the red was the test's.** The held-set clause at `:84` read `r.result.addressOf`, the pre-mint map. The
  pre-round file's own C-0274 test already pins that this map collides before the mint (`pair.test.ts` before-image
  :214 – :219, the f2 case). The round's change to the clause makes it read `r.minted.addressOf`, the addresses after
  the hand-on and the mint, and keeps the same claim: one holder per address, survivors included. That is a correction
  of what the clause reads, not a loosening of what it claims. CONFIRMED (diff) and PLAUSIBLE (the judgement).

**The required changes, one by one:**

| required change | outcome | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `pair.test.ts` green on the design tree at seed 1 | **met**, CONFIRMED | NEAR on the tree: `bench/test/determinism` 9 files, 60/60, exit 0; `pair.test.ts` holds 12 tests, all green. |
| uniqueness enforced in `mintAddresses` (an old id to at most one fresh holder, never to a successor when a fresh entity minted it) | **met**, CONFIRMED | `lawfulHandOn` gives the handed-on address only to the fresh entity that a `succeed` outcome of that address names. Every lawful hand-on is reserved before any natural address is minted. Any other hand-on is listed in `refused` and minted fresh. Under §6.3 the successor keeps the address and the natural holder takes `~k`; the round reads the row's phrase that way (C-0449 (2)), and this checker agrees that the design's text supports it. Mutants K2, K9, K12 and K15 are killed. |
| `duplicateIds` counts the case | **met**, CONFIRMED | It adds `refused.length`, and it counts any address held twice on the minted map. On the raw map the natural-holder pin counts 1 (`:302`). K5 and K14 are killed. |
| `silentRebinds` counts the case | **met**, CONFIRMED | It reads the final addresses too. A fresh entity ending at an old address it was not handed counts (`:303`). So does a refused hand-on of a held id (`:326`), and so does a mint that loses a hand-on (`:307`). K6, K7 and K8 are killed. |
| a PIN red without the fix (the seed-1 pair itself, named, or a planted held-id succession) | **met**, CONFIRMED | (a) The seed-1 pair: K16 (Q124's fault: `taken` holds only survivors and no hand-on is reserved, so a natural holder keeps a handed address) is red at `pair.test.ts:77:28`, `expected 2 to be +0`: the two successions above. (b) The planted pins ("a planted succession that hands a held id is refused …", and the fast-check property) are red on the before-image mint, which has no `refused` and keeps any hand-on as handed. K2 and K9 re-introduce that fault and are red at `:320` and `:321`. |
| if the cause is `match`'s, REPORT it | **not applicable**, CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE | The cause was not `match` (above). The notes say so, and say the pin passes with the guard alone. |
| the notes section states which it was; Q124's declared red lifts | **met**, CONFIRMED | `checks/M0-d-09-notes.md`, section 'Hardening round S2': "Which it was: neither the matcher nor the mint's output … The test." `pair.test.ts` is green on the tree. |

**The line is FIXED. Q124 can go DONE at this landing, and its declared red lifts.**

Not a Q124 promise: uniqueness holds under it, since one old id has one outcome naming one fresh entity. It is reachable only through a planted result, because `match` pairs within a kind. → note 14 (M4) |
| K5 | `duplicateIds` without `refused.length` | KILLED: `:259`, `:325` |
| K6 | the succession check in `silentRebinds` reads the raw map only | KILLED: `:307` (the lost hand-on) |
| K7 | `silentRebinds` blind to a fresh entity ending at an old address not handed to it | KILLED: `:303` |
| K8 | `silentRebinds` blind to a refused hand-on of a held id | KILLED: `:326` |
| K9 | a refused entity keeps its handed address | KILLED: `:259`, `:321` |
| K10 | the reservation's `taken.add(handed)` removed | survived; **equivalent**: a lawful hand-on is an old id, which `taken` holds from the start |
| K12 | no hand-on is ever lawful | KILLED, 8 tests: `:77` 392 duplicates |
| K13 | the kept-reference check in `silentRebinds` reads the raw map only | survived; **count-only**: a kept reference's `fresh` is its `succeed` outcome's, so the succession line (`:266`) counts the same case. The counter stays non-zero and the gate (`=== 0`) is unchanged → note 15 (M4) |
| K14 | `duplicateIds` reads the provisional ids, not the minted ones | KILLED: `:187`, `:227` |
| K15 | the second pass re-mints the successors | KILLED, 8 tests: `:78` 673 |
| K16 | Q124's fault (K1 + K10: the natural holder keeps the handed id) | KILLED: `:77:28` `expected 2 to be +0` (the seed-1 pair's two successions), `:188`, `:235` |

Result: 16 mutants. 12 were killed, 2 are equivalent (K3, K10), 1 is count-only (K13), and 1 is a non-Q124 survivor
(K4), routed as a hardening note. None of the survivors sits on a promise the row states.
